panels.description: Whether the cluster is green (all shards allocated), yellow (replicas unassigned), or red (primary shards unassigned).
panels.title: Cluster Status

panels.description: Total number of nodes in the cluster (data + master + coordinating).
panels.title: Total Nodes

panels.description: Number of data nodes currently in the cluster.
panels.title: Data Nodes

panels.description: Total number of active primary and replica shards across the cluster.
panels.title: Active Shards

panels.description: Number of active primary shards. Compare with total active shards to gauge replica ratio.
panels.title: Primary Shards

panels.description: Shards that exist but are not allocated to any node. Non-zero indicates capacity or configuration issues.
panels.title: Unassigned Shards

panels.description: Total number of documents indexed across all indices.
panels.title: Total Documents

panels.description: Total size of all indices on disk.
panels.title: Store Size

panels.description: Rate of documents being indexed per second.
panels.title: Indexing Rate (docs/s)

panels.description: Rate of search queries executed per second.
panels.title: Search Rate (queries/s)

panels.description: Average time to index a single document. High values indicate resource pressure or complex mappings.
panels.title: Indexing Latency

panels.description: Average time to execute a search query. High values may indicate slow queries, large result sets, or resource contention.
panels.title: Search Latency

panels.description: Average time for the fetch phase of a search (retrieving document content after scoring).
panels.title: Fetch Latency

panels.description: Time spent throttling indexing operations. Non-zero means writes are being actively slowed to allow merges to catch up.
panels.title: Indexing Throttle Time (rate)

panels.description: Rate of segment merge operations and number of currently running merges.
panels.title: Merge Rate & Current

panels.description: Rate of data being merged — high values compete with indexing for disk I/O.
panels.title: Merge Throughput (bytes/s)

panels.description: Rate of refresh and flush operations. High refresh rate affects search latency; high flush rate indicates I/O pressure.
panels.title: Refresh & Flush Rate

panels.description: Rate of scroll operations per node.
panels.title: Scroll Rate

panels.description: Whether indexing is being throttled on each node. 1 = throttled, 0 = normal.
panels.title: Indexing Throttled

panels.description: JVM heap utilization per node. Sustained values above 75% increase GC pressure; above 90% risks OOM.
panels.title: JVM Heap Used (%)

panels.description: Memory committed to the JVM heap — should be stable under normal operations.
panels.title: JVM Heap Committed

panels.description: Rate of JVM garbage collection cycles per node. Frequent old-gen GC indicates heap pressure.
panels.title: GC Collection Rate (/s)

panels.description: Time spent in garbage collection per second.
panels.title: GC Duration (s/s)

panels.description: OS-level CPU utilization per node.
panels.title: CPU Usage (%)

panels.description: Operating system memory usage per node.
panels.title: OS Memory Usage

panels.description: Disk usage percentage per node. OpenSearch triggers shard relocation at 85% and blocks writes at 90%.
panels.title: Disk Usage (%)

panels.description: Available disk space per node. Watch for nodes dropping below ~20 GiB (or 25% of per-node storage) — OpenSearch blocks writes as disks fill.
panels.title: Free Storage Space (GiB)

panels.description: Disk read/write throughput on data nodes.
panels.title: Disk I/O

panels.description: Inter-node transport layer traffic for replication and search.
panels.title: Network Transport I/O

panels.description: 1-minute load average per node. Values above CPU count indicate saturation.
panels.title: OS Load Average (1m)

panels.description: File descriptor usage as percentage of OS limit. Approaching 100% causes index failures and node instability.
panels.title: File Descriptors Used (%)

panels.description: Current queue depth for the busiest thread pools. Growing queues precede rejections.
panels.title: Thread Pool Queue Size (top active)

panels.description: Rate of rejected operations per thread pool. Rejections mean the queue is full and work is being dropped.
panels.title: Thread Pool Rejected (rate)

panels.description: Currently active threads per pool. Shows current parallelism across thread pools.
panels.title: Thread Pool Active (top)

panels.description: Queued tasks in the write thread pool per node. Sustained values above ~100 indicate high indexing concurrency — review indexing load or scale the cluster.
panels.title: Write Thread Pool Queue

panels.description: Queued tasks in the search thread pool per node. Sustained values above ~500 (and especially ~5000) indicate high search concurrency — consider scaling the cluster or increasing the search queue.
panels.title: Search Thread Pool Queue

panels.description: Rate of rejected tasks in the write thread pool. Any sustained increase means indexing requests are being dropped — review load or scale the cluster.
panels.title: Write Thread Pool Rejections (rate)

panels.description: Rate of rejected tasks in the search thread pool. Any sustained increase means search requests are being dropped — consider scaling the cluster.
panels.title: Search Thread Pool Rejections (rate)

panels.description: Rate of circuit breaker trips per breaker type. Trips protect against OOM by rejecting requests that would exceed memory limits.
panels.title: Circuit Breaker Tripped (rate)

panels.description: Current memory usage as a percentage of the circuit breaker limit. Approaching 100% means trips are imminent.
panels.title: Circuit Breaker Memory Usage (%)

panels.description: Number of shards currently initializing. Non-zero values indicate recovery or rebalancing is in progress.
panels.title: Initializing Shards

panels.description: Number of shards being moved between nodes. Non-zero indicates cluster rebalancing activity.
panels.title: Relocating Shards

panels.description: Number of shards whose allocation has been delayed by the cluster settings.
panels.title: Delayed Unassigned Shards

panels.description: Number of cluster-level pending tasks waiting to be executed. A growing count indicates the master node is overloaded.
panels.title: Pending Tasks

panels.description: Percentage of query cache lookups that result in a hit.
panels.title: Query Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Request cache hit rate. The request cache stores results of whole shard-level search requests.
panels.title: Request Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Memory consumed by query cache and request cache.
panels.title: Cache Memory

panels.description: Rate of cache evictions. High eviction rates mean the cache is too small for the working set.
panels.title: Cache Evictions (rate)

panels.description: Memory consumed by fielddata per node. Fielddata is used for sorting and aggregations on text fields and can grow unbounded.
panels.title: Fielddata Memory

panels.description: Number of Lucene segments per node. High segment counts increase search latency and memory usage until merges consolidate them.
panels.title: Segment Count

panels.description: Memory consumed by segment metadata (term dictionaries, stored fields, etc.).
panels.title: Segment Memory

panels.description: Number of operations in the translog awaiting flush. Large translogs increase recovery time after a node restart.
panels.title: Translog Operations

panels.description: Size of the translog on disk. Correlates with recovery time and can indicate flush tuning needs.
panels.title: Translog Size

panels.description: Total number of documents stored on each node. Useful for detecting uneven data distribution across the cluster.
panels.title: Documents Count per Node

panels.description: Number of deleted documents not yet purged by segment merges. High counts may inflate storage and slow searches.
panels.title: Documents Deleted
OpenSearch Vended Metrics (aws.es) — requires CloudWatch vended-metric enrichment

panels.description: Whether the cluster is blocking incoming write requests (AWS/ES ClusterIndexWritesBlocked). 0 = accepting, 1 = blocking. Usually caused by low free storage or high JVM memory pressure.
panels.title: Cluster Index Writes Blocked

panels.description: Number of failed automated snapshots (AWS/ES AutomatedSnapshotFailure). A value of 1 means no automated snapshot was taken in the previous 36 hours, often due to a red cluster status.
panels.title: Automated Snapshot Failure

panels.description: KMS encryption-key health (AWS/ES KMSKeyError / KMSKeyInaccessible). 1 = the key used for encryption at rest is disabled (KMSKeyError) or deleted/revoked (KMSKeyInaccessible). Only published for domains that encrypt data at rest.
panels.title: KMS Key Errors

panels.description: Old-generation heap usage across data nodes (AWS/ES OldGenJVMMemoryPressure). Sustained values above ~80% indicate risk of out-of-memory even when overall heap looks healthy.
panels.title: Old Gen JVM Memory Pressure (%)

panels.description: CPU usage on dedicated master nodes (AWS/ES MasterCPUUtilization). Master nodes should stay well below data nodes; sustained values above ~50% warrant a larger master instance type.
panels.title: Master CPU Utilization (%)

panels.description: Heap usage on dedicated master nodes (AWS/ES MasterJVMMemoryPressure). Sustained values above ~95% risk out-of-memory on the masters — consider a larger master instance type.
panels.title: Master JVM Memory Pressure (%)

panels.description: Old-generation heap usage on dedicated master nodes (AWS/ES MasterOldGenJVMMemoryPressure). Sustained values above ~80% indicate memory pressure on the masters.
panels.title: Master Old Gen JVM Memory Pressure (%)

panels.description: Health check for MasterNotDiscovered exceptions (AWS/ES MasterReachableFromNode). 1 = normal. A value of 0 means the master node is unreachable, usually a network or AWS dependency problem.
panels.title: Master Reachable From Node

panels.description: Share of requests returning HTTP 5xx (AWS/ES 5xx / OpenSearchRequests). Sustained values above ~10% suggest overloaded data nodes or requests failing within the idle timeout — consider larger instances or more nodes.
panels.title: 5xx Errors (% of requests)
